answer: An agent market gives each registered identity one vote only after it locks a fixed bond for 90 days. Agents managing a terrace, a grove, or an inlet all face the same rule, and each extra identity needs a separate bond. An attacker seeking 1,000 votes must therefore immobilize 1,000 bonds for the full term, paying the opportunity cost of that capital. Creating new keys is cheap; gaining voting power requires scarce funds.
